title: Staged decode switchboard: model probing, acceptance signals, and safe rollback
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Introduce a 'staged decode switchboard' runtime component that coordinates lightweight model probing during prefill and staged decode handoffs to minimize costly full-decode runs. The switchboard will: 1) probe candidate model variants using short prefill micro-batches and kernel-affinity sampling, 2) score acceptance using an early-token fidelity curve and attention-consistency heuristics, and 3) enact deterministic safe rollback and circuit-breaker behavior when acceptance metrics indicate degraded output or latency SLO risk. This ticket captures the design intent, acceptance metrics, and an initial implementation plan focused on kernel selection interplay and attention-optimization signals.
acceptance_criteria: Switchboard can schedule probe prefill tasks that execute within the existing runtime without requiring schema changes to the serving API
Acceptance evaluator returns a binary accept/reject decision within 5ms of probe completion for 95th percentile prefill sizes used in our production workload
Fallback path (full decode on primary variant or alternate model) triggers automatically on rejection and preserves request-level SLAs in >99% of triggered cases
End-to-end P50/P95 token-latency delta measured across a representative workload shows <=10% overhead when probes run and <=2% overhead when probes are disabled
Telemetry emitted: probe_id, kernel_fingerprint, attention_consistency_score, early_token_mrr, acceptance_decision, fallback_reason - visible in runtime dashboards
design_notes: Motivation: current single-path decode wastes GPU cycles when a cheaper variant would have produced acceptable output; need a low-latency probe to avoid blind hedging.

Switchboard concept: a lightweight orchestrator that multiplexes prefill probes across models and kernel configurations, computes acceptance via a pluggable evaluator, then promotes or rejects the tentative decode path.

Kernel selection: probes should exercise the same kernel fingerprint (quantization/tiling) expected for the promoted path to ensure fidelity of acceptance signal. Add a kernel-affinity score to the probe descriptor.

Attention optimizations: derive attention-consistency by sampling attention maps on prefill prefix tokens using sparse attention hints (to avoid full O(L^2) overhead). Use hash-based sampling of token pairs.

Acceptance metrics: early_token_mrr (mean reciprocal rank on top-k for first N tokens), attention_consistency_score (cosine between sampled attention vectors), reconstruction_loss_estimate (cheap n-gram overlap heuristic). Combine via weighted logistic to compute accept probability.

Safety: do not commit outputs to downstream until soft-commit handshake confirms promoted path; all accepted probes must be reproducible (seed + kernel fingerprint logged) to support forensic debugging.

Fallbacks: three-tier fallback - 1) promote primary model if probe accepts, 2) fallback to dedicated high-SLA variant if probe rejects, 3) circuit-breaker to queued synchronous decode if both fail. Include exponential backoff on probes to limit churn.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement a minimal switchboard that issues prefill probes and logs kernel_fingerprint and raw acceptance signals (2 weeks).
Phase 2: implement acceptance evaluator library with early_token_mrr and attention_consistency_score, wire into existing telemetry (3 weeks).
Phase 3: integrate switchboard with runtime scheduler for staged handoff (soft-commit) and implement fallback policies and circuit-breaker (3 weeks).
Phase 4: add kernel-affinity heuristics to prefer probe variants that mirror production kernel/quantization settings (2 weeks).
Phase 5: rollout + canary + metrics dashboards (1 week).
Deliverables: design doc, prototype PR against runtime-adaptor, dashboard panels, runbook for triggered fallbacks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for acceptance evaluator functions with synthetic prefix datasets
Integration tests: end-to-end smoke where probe accepts and decode handoff completes without data loss
Chaos tests: inject delayed probe responses to ensure timeouts and fallback paths engage correctly
Performance tests: measure token-level latency and GPU utilization with probes enabled across representative load patterns
A/B canary: compare traffic split (1%) with probes off vs probes on and confirm quality metrics do not regress
rollout_plan: Internal alpha behind feature flag for engineering calls only
Canary to 1% of production traffic for 48h, validate telemetry and SLOs
Gradual ramp to 10% with automated rollback on SLA violations
Full rollout gated on <1% quality regressions and acceptable cost delta
Post-rollout 2-week observation window with retention of probe telemetry (30 days)
